capabilities.gap: Productive selection remains fail-closed when the immutable release artifact or approval key material does not match.
Deployment-specific tenant and worker capacity values remain bounded configuration and are exposed through Hub health/evidence.
Only commonly supported plans are compared; unsupported capabilities remain explicitly incompatible rather than synthetically equivalent.
The SQL store is authoritative; deployment admission still verifies the applied migration head and signing-key availability.
Each deployment must still retain its own restart/restore evidence even though Hub and worker replacement contracts are automated.
Consumers must use the authenticated Hub cursor; direct worker streams are intentionally unsupported.
Only versioned, prevalidated components may be promoted; runtime-local executable component code is intentionally rejected.
Dry-run is evidence-only and suppresses all side effects; it can never substitute for a required live capability.
The worker executes only a predelegated node; run control and task fan-out intentionally remain in the Hub.
Only the shared typed side-effect-free condition language is supported; free Python/template routing is intentionally incompatible.
Legacy adapter resume tokens are development-only; production accepts only signed, role-bound Hub commands and SQL checkpoints.
Runtime-private state remains diagnostic only and cannot override canonical Hub events or a signed Hub checkpoint.
Review decisions remain Hub-owned and require current checkpoint, plan, policy, actor role and approval evidence bindings.
Local MemorySaver remains an explicit development-only restriction; productive runs require the Hub-owned SQL checkpoint gateway.
Every request remains tenant/source-allowlist bound; an absent or unknown supplied source identifier fails as unverified.
Automated replay and real Compose recovery are present; each production deployment must still retain environment-specific backup/restore evidence.
Requires mounted keyrings, service authentication and Hub availability.
Uncertain non-idempotent outcomes intentionally remain blocked until Hub ledger reconciliation resolves them.
Public control remains Hub-authenticated and tenant-bound; direct Temporal commands are unsupported.
Cancel/write races are fenced and reconciled; unresolved external effects intentionally remain uncertain rather than reported as cancelled success.
Unknown versions and stale/inconsistent projections block promotion.
The repository N-1 corpus is release-blocking; deployment-specific histories and candidate Build IDs remain required rollout evidence.
